baer-heitev/1:ג: Whose absorption is slight — such as spoons and cups; one must be concerned that they will absorb from what the bowls and pots expel.
baer-heitev/1:ו: That he insert — so that it not absorb from the hagalah water.
baer-heitev/1:ז: And last — meaning when one kashered it at the beginning or at the end.
baer-heitev/2:ג: Forbidden food — that there must be that it is not ben yomo or sixty in the water against it, and then it is permitted to kasher even a forbidden vessel first.
baer-heitev/3:_: Touching — and regarding tevilat kelim there is no concern {Rama: (for there it depends on chatzitzah)}. See Beit Yosef.
baer-heitev/4:_: With tongs — Orach U'Mussar wrote: it is better to place it in small woven strings of fish or in a basket — end of his words. Kaf HaChayyim.
baer-heitev/5:ב: To kasher more — and b'dieved it is permitted as with other liquids; requires study — Kaf HaChayyim. Orach U'Mussar wrote that one may not use hagalah water of forbidden food l'chatchila even if there is sixty against the vessel, because it is like nullifying prohibition l'chatchila since one wants to use the water.
baer-heitev/7:_: To rinse — and b'dieved there is no concern if one did not rinse at all. Kaf HaChayyim.
machatzit-hashekel/3:א: (s.k. 3) However etc. — for Rabbeinu Yehuda also agrees to this even before the time of prohibition hagalah does not help in water at yad soledes bo unless it raises boiling.
machatzit-hashekel/5:_: (s.k. 5) First etc. — meaning when one wants to use the pot on Pesach; but because of the vessels one kasher in it, the pot needs no hagalah at all.
magen-avraham/1:ב: Whose absorption is slight — such as spoons and cups; one must be concerned they will absorb from what bowls and pots expel.
magen-avraham/1:ד: And similarly if one leaves them too long — one must be concerned that after finishing expulsion it will again absorb from hagalah water.
magen-avraham/1:ה: And similarly so that one need not be careful — that the water not cease boiling.
magen-avraham/2:א: Together — meaning one inserts them at once into the pot and there is not sixty in the pot against any one of them.
magen-avraham/2:ב: Unless one of them — or there is sixty against it; all this during the rest of the year or on erev Pesach before the fifth hour; not so afterward — one must be careful in each that it not be ben yomo or sixty, as explained.
magen-avraham/5:_: In no drink. "The water that is involved with Ephraim, which is cohesed with a blasphemy."
magen-avraham/6:ג: A boiling stone. The water filter:
mechaber/1:main: The time for kashering vessels. Containg 7 sections: One should be cautious to kasher vessels prior to the fifth hour so that one need not be particular if the vessels have been used in the past day or not and similarly if one is kashering vessels which have absorbed a small amount of food together with vessels that have absorbed a large amount of food, and similarly if the vessels were left in the vat excessively, or if the vessels were not left [in the vat] sufficiently and similarly so that he need not be concerned that the water ceased boiling. , and [one need not be particular] that he entered the vessel prior to the water boiling and similarly so that he doesn't have to kasher the large vat before and after kashering. {Rama: (or if [he is kashering with] at least 60 times the volume of the vessel of water or not (Tur) {Rama: there are many who dispute this and they would say that no kashering whatsoever was effected if the water ceased boiling (and similarly is evident from the Rosh, the Smag and the T"H in siman 131 and Agur and Tur in siman 105). Based on this, there are those who are cautious, even prior to the time chametz becomes forbidden, so that the water shouldn't cease the boiling during the entire time of kashering (Own words) {Rama: and if he didn't kasher prior to the beginning of the time when chametz becomes forbidden, he is able to kasher until Pesach itself. When there is a minute amount of chametz, kashering doesn't positively affect it because it will return and reabsorb, rather, it is permitted to incandesce a vessel during Pesach. (His own words and Teshuvat Rashba} When one is kashering after the sixth hour but prior to Pesach one must be cautious regarding all of the information described [above] whereas it is not necessary to be cautious prior to the sixth hour.}
mechaber/2:main: One should be cautious when kashering a meat vessel and a dairy vessel together unless one of them was not used in the past day. {Rama: (And certainly regarding a forbidden food vessel and based on this, it is customary to not kasher vessels which have been used in the past day.)}
mechaber/3:main: A number of vessels should not be placed inside of a single vessel and then kashered together {Rama: (if there is contact between them)}
mechaber/4:main: If he kashers with forceps, he should rotate the vessel lest the area clamped by the forceps not be sufficiently contacted by the boiling water.
mechaber/5:main: One may not kasher in the hot-springs of Tevaria, even vessels which have the status of secondary vessels, because the heat is not born out from a fire. That which is absorbed is similarly ejected and just as [the food] is absorbed through heat born out from fire, so to it is ejected through heat born out from a fire. {Rama: {Rama: However, if it's usage is only in the waters of Tevaria, then it may be kashered there (Beis Yosef in the name of A"CH). One may not kasher with any liquids except water, however, post-facto, kashering is achieved with all liquids (Beis Yosef in the name of A"CH}. If one kashers many vessels in the vat to the extent that the combined discharge from the vessels has made the water saucy, one may kasher no further [vessels] with this water (Ra"n on "Kol haBasar")}
mechaber/6:main: [Regarding] A vessels which large to the extent that it cannot fit inside of another vessel because of its size, one should make a lip of clay around the mouth of the vessel to the extent that it can be filled up well and the water will reach the lip. [The vessel] should then be filled with water and boiled, or one should take a hot stone or burning torch and place it inside when the water is boiling and the water inside will be further boiled and will ascend to the lip.
mechaber/7:main: It is customary to rinse the vessel in cold water immediately after kashering it.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (1) One should be careful etc. — the reason: hagalah works by boiling water expelling what was absorbed in the vessel; but one must be concerned that after expelling the absorption it will return and absorb in the vessel what it expelled; because of this concern poskim wrote one may kasher only a vessel that is not ben yomo, for then even if it absorbs what it expelled it is noten taam lifgam, or there should be sixty in the water to nullify the expulsion of prohibition; and on this the Mechaber says that if one kasher before the fifth hour one need not be careful in all this, for then it is still the time of chametz heter and it is noten taam bar noten taam d'heter — meaning the chametz taste the vessels received initially was heter taste, and the water taste they now receive from the vessels is also heter, and what returns and gives taste in vessels is also heter.
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (3) Whose absorption is slight etc. — such as spoons and cups with bowls and pots; one must be concerned that after they finish expelling their slight absorption they will return and absorb from the expulsion of other vessels whose absorption is great; but before the fifth hour, which is entirely heter, one need not be concerned even if they absorb, for it is noten taam bar noten taam d'heter.
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (4) And similarly if one leaves them etc. and does not etc. — meaning if one kasher a forbidden vessel to kasher it or a chametz vessel after the time of prohibition one must be precise not to leave them long in the water, for one must be concerned that after finishing expulsion it will return and absorb; and also not to leave them at all but remove immediately is not correct, for one must leave a little until it expels its absorption, and this is hard to measure; but if one kasher them before the time of prohibition one need not measure and may leave them longer in the water [and if one kasher them after the time of prohibition — from the fifth hour on erev Pesach until evening, or generally a forbidden vessel — one must be precise that the vessel not be ben yomo or that there be sixty in the water to nullify the absorption, for then also there is no concern if one leaves them long in the water].
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (5) That the water not cease boiling etc. — meaning all the time they are boiling they are busy expelling and do not absorb from hagalah water; and when they cease boiling they absorb.
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (6) However many dispute etc. — Acharonim challenged the Rama, for the Mechaber view is also that hagalah helps only when the water is boiling; rather he wrote that after the time of prohibition it is forbidden to leave the vessels after the water ceases boiling, for then they return and absorb from hagalah water; not so beforehand — one need not be concerned for this since the hagalah itself was at the time of their boiling.
mishnah-berurah/1:ז: (7) If the water is not boiling — meaning even if yad soledes bo, all the time the water does not raise boiling they do not expel.
mishnah-berurah/1:ח: (8) All the time one is kashering — meaning the large pot in which one places vessels every hour to kasher — the water should not cease boiling all the time one continues kashering in it, for a vessel one places there after the water ceased boiling — hagalah does not ascend to it [unless one leaves the vessel in it until the water boils again]. The nature of water is that it ceases boiling when one inserts cold vessels to kasher; therefore one must wait in each vessel until the water bubbles; and one must warn those who kasher, for they practice lightly and kasher quickly one after another and do not check if boiling rises; and one may learn merit for them, for the way of kashering is only bowls and spoons used by irui, for which hagalah in water at yad soledes bo alone helps; however in a copper pot and things whose use is via kli rishon it appears that even b'dieved this hagalah does not help and one must return and kasher [but regarding forbidding the food if one used it on Pesach the Peri Megadim is uncertain; and it appears if it is not ben yomo from when chametz was used in it one may lean lenient]; Acharonim wrote it is proper to place at hagalah a Torah scholar expert in hagalah laws.
mishnah-berurah/1:ט: (9) And that one not insert etc. — meaning if one kasher after the time of prohibition it is not proper to insert the vessel before the water boils, even if one leaves it inside until it boils, lest it absorb then from hagalah water containing vessels expulsion [and even though afterward when the water boils it will also expel this absorption — nevertheless l'chatchila one should not add chametz absorption]; not so if one kasher before the time of prohibition — one need not be concerned for this.
mishnah-berurah/1:י: (10) So that one need not etc. — meaning if one kasher after the time of prohibition one must kasher first the pot in which one kasher vessels, pour out the hagalah water, boil other water in it, and insert the vessels [for if one does not kasher it first, the water in the pot becomes forbidden from the pot, for there is not sixty in the water against the whole pot, and the forbidden water returns and forbids the vessels kashered in it]; and also at the end after kashering all vessels, when one wants to use the pot, one must kasher it again so it expels hagalah water absorbed in it; not so if one kasher vessels before the time of prohibition — one need not kasher the pot first, for then it is noten taam bar noten taam d'heter as above; and only if one wants to use the pot after the time of prohibition must one kasher it at the end.
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (15) To kasher — and even before the fifth hour, since it is because of meat and milk.
mishnah-berurah/2:ג: (16) Together — meaning one inserts them at one time into the pot; the reason is that meat and milk expulsions mix together and are absorbed in the vessels and become forbidden.
mishnah-berurah/2:ד: (17) One of them etc. — ben yomo is permitted, for it receives from what is not ben yomo only impaired taste; and what is not ben yomo is also permitted, for the taste absorbed from ben yomo is noten taam bar noten taam d'heter and is not considered taste; and after hagalah one may use each for what he wants — meat or milk.
mishnah-berurah/2:ו: (19) Forbidden vessel — meaning even though one kasher it itself one must be careful that it not be ben yomo from when forbidden food was used in it, or that there be sixty in the water against it, lest it become forbidden if it again absorbs its expulsion.
mishnah-berurah/3:א: (21) Into a vessel — meaning a perforated basket or net; in a non-perforated vessel one may not kasher even one vessel, even when it floats and does not touch the bottom, unless one leaves them in the pot until the water raises boiling in the vessel one wants to kasher.
mishnah-berurah/4:_: (23) One should rotate the vessel — meaning one opens the tongs inside the boiling water and grasps the vessel in another place so boiling rises on the place the tongs held. It is better to kasher in a net or perforated basket.
mishnah-berurah/5:א: (24) One may kasher in them — or in hot-spring waters.
mishnah-berurah/5:ב: (25) In any liquid — for their nature is not to expel absorption.
mishnah-berurah/5:ג: (26) However b'dieved — because some dispute that liquids also expel like water, and we rely on them for b'dieved; and poskim wrote the same regarding water mixed with ashes called lye, or what smiths practice heating the vessel via wine lees or vinegar-stein mixed in water — one may not kasher in them l'chatchila, only in water alone; b'dieved hagalah helps in them; and see in Peri Megadim whose view is that if it is before Pesach one should kasher a second time in water alone; however if Pesach arrived it is permitted l'chatchila to use this hagalah.
mishnah-berurah/5:ד: (27) One may kasher no more — for they no longer have power to expel absorption; and it is possible that even b'dieved this hagalah does not help.
mishnah-berurah/5:ה: (28) In that water — and even if one kashered in them vessels that are not ben yomo, the law is the same.
mishnah-berurah/6:א: (29) A large vessel etc. — meaning one wants to kasher it and is concerned perhaps there is chametz absorption on its lip where the water does not reach; and the same law for a pot after one kashered vessels in it and wants to use it on Pesach — one must make a lip or white-hot stone; but initially before kashering the vessels and kashering the pot first from the prohibition in it — one need not make a lip.
mishnah-berurah/6:ב: (30) One makes a lip at its mouth — meaning around its mouth and not on it directly, for the vessel mouth must be exposed so boiling water reaches there.
mishnah-berurah/6:ד: (32) Or one takes — meaning one fills it well at first.
mishnah-berurah/6:ה: (33) A white-hot stone — for cold cools the water.
turei-zahav/1:א: Before the fifth hour — for then it is noten taam bar noten taam d'heter; and in some Tur manuscripts it is written before six.
turei-zahav/1:ג: That they not cease boiling — and if they ceased, then one boils again and kasher in them, and the pot is not forbidden from what the water ceased.
turei-zahav/2:ב: Therefore the practice is not to kasher — meaning even if one kasher one vessel.
turei-zahav/3:_: If they touch one another — for at the place of contact boiling does not reach, even though regarding tevilah there is no chatzitzah prohibition here; regarding boiling it is different — so Mordechai in the name of Rokeach; but because of vessel expulsion prohibition there is no concern even if they are ben yomo, for it is noten taam bar noten taam d'heter — before six, like fish that rose in a meat bowl that is permitted to eat with kutach, as Yoreh De'ah siman 97.
baer-heitev/1:א: The fifth hour — meaning from the beginning of the fifth hour until the end of the fourth hour, for since from the fourth hour it is forbidden in any case d'rabbanan, it is no longer called noten taam bar noten taam d'heter. {Rama: (And regarding the reason of chametz some say it returns and reawakens; and for b'dieved see Yoreh De'ah siman 95 seif 3)} Acharonim.
baer-heitev/1:ב: Beit Yosef — that even though the vessel is ben yomo and there is not sixty in the water against it, nevertheless it is permitted because it is noten taam bar noten taam d'heter, which is not so after the fifth hour; and even though above in siman 447 seif 5 the Rama forbids things cooked in their vessels and does not permit from the reason of noten taam bar noten taam — here there are many taste transfers from food to vessel and from vessel to water and from water to vessel, and it returns and expels from the vessel into the cooked food during Pesach — Magen Avraham. {Rama: (And Kaf HaChayyim wrote that in cooking we forbid l'chatchila noten taam bar noten taam, and it is like l'chatchila since it is possible to wait)} Kaf HaChayyim.
baer-heitev/1:ד: And he does not leave them — this phrase has no explanation or relevance at all. See Kaf HaChayyim who resolves it.
baer-heitev/1:ה: Dispute — the words of the Rama are puzzling, for the Rabbeinu Yehuda also agrees to this, except that after its prohibition, once the water ceases boiling it is forbidden to boil them a second time, for all the time they are boiling they did not absorb from the hagalah water; and if they ceased boiling they absorbed; but before the time of prohibition one may boil them a second time and kasher in it, for it is noten taam bar noten taam d'heter. Magen Avraham and Kaf HaChayyim.
baer-heitev/1:ח: In any amount — because of chol ha-moed he needed this reason, for on Yom Tov itself, even on other Yamim Tovim, it is forbidden to kasher, as written siman 509 Taz.
baer-heitev/1:ט: Six — meaning not only after six but even after four one must be careful, as written s.k. 1.
baer-heitev/1:י: The matters etc. — meaning one should see that the vessels not be ben yomo; and if they are ben yomo there must be sixty in the water against it; and if one kasher many vessels one after another there must be sixty against all of them, for the prohibition returns and reawakens; and if one vessel absorbed meat and the other fish it does not return and reawaken since they are distinct tastes; and one should kasher first vessels whose absorption is slight and afterward vessels whose absorption is great; and one should not leave them too long; and the water should not cease boiling; and one should kasher the pot first and last. Magen Avraham wrote: it appears to me that if the pot is not ben yomo one need not kasher it first, for it is no worse than the vessel itself; and if one kashered it at the beginning one need not kasher it at the end, for the vessels are not ben yomo; nevertheless the practice is to be stringent in all stringencies even before the fifth hour — so too Bach. Maharil and Mateh Moshe and Minhagim wrote that one should kasher three days before Pesach. Shaarei Chaim siman 470 wrote: a Torah scholar expert in hagalah should kasher — this is correct — end of Kaf HaChayyim.
baer-heitev/2:א: Together — meaning that one inserts them at one time into the pot and there is not sixty in the pot against any one of them. For b'dieved see Yoreh De'ah siman 95 seif 6. And see siman 509 in Magen Avraham small seif 11 the reason for those who practice not to kasher a dairy vessel to eat meat in it or vice versa.
baer-heitev/2:ב: Ben yomo — or there is sixty against it. All this is during the rest of the year or on erev Pesach before the fifth hour; but afterward one must be careful in each of them that it not be ben yomo or that there be sixty, as explained.
baer-heitev/2:ד: Any vessel — even alone and before the fifth hour, and even if there is sixty, because of a decree regarding a forbidden vessel that hagalah does not help for it all the time it is ben yomo, for it returns and absorbs from the hagalah water, and noten taam bar noten taam d'heter does not apply to it {Rama: (And Shach Yoreh De'ah siman 95 asks from what we say there: a meat bowl rinsed in a pot of milk is permitted; and he answered that there it is b'dieved; and Peri Chadash rejected his view — is it not noten taam bar noten taam d'heter? Rather he concludes that the stringency l'chatchila is per the view of poskim that taste of two substances mixes at once in the water)}. Magen Avraham wrote: even counters one should scrub well and wait after scrubbing twenty-four hours so they not be ben yomo, and they should be dried from cold water lest they be cooled from the boiling ones; and one should be careful to pour on them quickly, not by throwing in the air, for that is not considered irui {Rama: (see Yoreh De'ah siman 95)}; and one should be careful to pour from the vessel in which one boiled the water and not draw with another vessel from the pot and pour on them to kasher, for that is called kli sheini; however if one leaves the vessel with which one draws inside the pot until the water raises its boiling, it is considered properly kli rishon — see Taz Yoreh De'ah siman 92 end of his words in the name of Maharil. See Kaf HaChayyim and see above siman 451 s.k. 43.
baer-heitev/5:א: Liquid — and the same applies in water with ashes called in Ashkenaz language lye; so too Beit Yosef and Peri Chadash Yoreh De'ah siman 95 s.k. 19; therefore that hagalah they do in their homes in a pewter vessel with white-hot stones with lye water is not properly called hagalah, especially since they do it when they are dirty; therefore one must be careful with those large vessels that one does not insert into the pot — one should clean them well with water alone — Kaf HaChayyim. And in Be'er Heitev which I annotated only in water, and wrote on it those mixed with ashes called lye — there it seems from his wording that the essence of hagalah is in lye water and he was not precise.
baer-heitev/6:_: With clay — even though the water drips through the clay. And the same applies to a pot in which one kashered vessels and wants to use it on Pesach — one must make a lip for it or a white-hot stone — Taz. A vessel whose use is from the outside, like a bowl that one sometimes inverts on a pot, or a vessel with which one draws from the pot — it has no remedy in this manner, for the outer side was not kashered; therefore one must insert it entirely into the pot — Magen Avraham. A vessel whose mouth is narrow so one cannot scrub inside, or that has cracks — forbidden in hagalah — Maharil; and see above siman 451 s.k. (43) [45].
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (2) Before the fifth hour — from the beginning of the fifth hour, since it is forbidden in any case d'rabbanan, it is no longer called noten taam bar noten taam d'heter.
mishnah-berurah/1:כ: (11) Until Pesach etc. — because of chol ha-moed he needed this reason, for on Yom Tov itself, even on other Yamim Tovim, it is forbidden to kasher, as below siman 509 [Taz].
mishnah-berurah/1:ל: (12) For then chametz is in any amount — meaning and hagalah does not help even if one wants to kasher it inside a large vessel that has sixty in its water against the vessel to nullify the expulsion; and even though the vessel is not ben yomo from when chametz was used in it, and also the large vessel is not ben yomo — nevertheless for us who hold siman 447 seif 10 to be stringent on Pesach even in noten taam lifgam — it is forbidden.
mishnah-berurah/1:מ: (13) After six — not specifically, for even after four one must be careful, as in s.k. 2; so wrote several Acharonim; except they wrote that what the Rama wrote that one must be careful in all matters is not specifically d'oraita until night in one of two matters as below; and some resolve that therefore he specified after six, for then it is proper to be careful in all matters mentioned in the Mechaber's words; not so if one kasher after four until six — it suffices to be careful in one of two matters: (a) see that the vessel one kasher and also the large pot in which one kasher are both not ben yomo; (b) if the vessel one kasher is ben yomo there must be sixty in the water against that whole vessel to nullify it [and if one kasher many vessels one after another there must be sixty in the water against all, for chametz prohibition in the expulsion returns and reawakens and joins together]; however if the large pot is ben yomo there is no remedy to kasher in it unless one kasher it beforehand per law, for the water in it does not have sixty against the vessel itself, as explained in Yoreh De'ah in several places. All this is d'oraita; but already the practice is l'chatchila to be stringent in all stringencies even if one kasher at the fourth hour or before [Magen Avraham and Bach]; and see in Biur Halacha where we explained in the name of several Acharonim who hold these two matters — requiring vessels not be ben yomo or sixty in water to nullify them — are d'oraita even before the time of chametz prohibition. It is permitted to kasher a forbidden knife in a kosher pot if there is sixty in the water against it and it is not nullifying prohibition, since one's intent is only to remove absorption; nevertheless one may not afterward use the water in the pot [Acharonim]; and see in Chokhmat Adam klal 47 seif 8.
mishnah-berurah/2:א: (14) One should be careful — and per Rama in Yoreh De'ah siman 95 seif 3 in the hagahah, even b'dieved it is forbidden.
mishnah-berurah/2:ה: (18) Is not ben yomo — and the same even if both are ben yomo but there is sixty against one vessel, for then its expulsion is nullified and it is as if it does not exist. All this during the rest of the year and because of meat-milk prohibition, or on erev Pesach before the fifth hour; not so afterward — one must be careful in each that it not be ben yomo or that there be sixty against all, as in s.k. 13.
mishnah-berurah/2:ז: (20) Any ben yomo vessel — meaning whether from meat to milk or chametz to matzah; even if one kasher it alone and before the fifth hour and there is sixty, because of a decree lest one kasher a forbidden vessel with less than sixty, for there hagalah does not help all the time it is ben yomo, for it returns and absorbs from hagalah water. And even counters one should scrub well and wait after scrubbing twenty-four hours so they not be ben yomo, and dried well from cold water lest they be cooled from boiling ones; and be careful to pour on them quickly, not by throwing in air, for that is not considered irui; and be careful to pour on them from the vessel in which one boiled the water, but not draw with another vessel from the pot and pour on them to kasher, for that is kli sheini — if one kasher without a white-hot stone — unless one leaves the vessel with which one draws inside the pot until the water raises boiling in a small pot, then it is properly kli rishon [Magen Avraham in the name of Maharil]; and see what we wrote above siman 451 in Mishna Berurah s.k. 114 in the name of Mahariw.
mishnah-berurah/3:ב: (22) If they touch one another — for at the place of contact boiling does not reach, even though regarding tevilah there is no chatzitzah; regarding boiling it is different.
mishnah-berurah/6:ג: (31) With clay — and during the rest of the year when one wants to kasher from prohibition one makes a lip of dough. The reason for making the lip is because it is impossible that boiling not splash once from chametz cooked in it onto the lip from above, and perhaps at hagalah time boiling water will not splash enough to expel chametz absorbed in it; therefore one makes the lip so water reaches there. All this in a vessel that cannot be inserted into a kli rishon of chametz but is used with boiling inside — therefore this remedy suffices; but a vessel used from outside, like a bowl sometimes inverted on a pot, or a vessel with which one draws from the pot — has no remedy this way, for the outer side was not kashered; therefore one must insert it entirely into the pot. A vessel whose mouth is narrow so one cannot scrub inside, or that has cracks [called rarerin] — forbidden in hagalah.
mishnah-berurah/7:_: (34) Immediately — so it not return and absorb from boiling water on it that contains chametz expulsion; nevertheless b'dieved even if one did not rinse at all one need not be concerned, for one kasher only before the time of prohibition, or it is not ben yomo, or there is sixty in the water against it, as above.
machatzit-hashekel/1:_: (s.k. 1) If etc. nevertheless permitted — meaning that if one kasher after the time of prohibition in such a manner hagalah does not help, for in such a case the hagalah water becomes forbidden from the expulsion of the vessels kashered in it; and after the vessel finishes its expulsion they return and absorb from the hagalah water; and even though the water did not cease boiling one may not rely on this, as written below; nevertheless before the time of prohibition there is no concern because it is noten taam etc. of things cooked in a chametz vessel and not etc. as should be.
machatzit-hashekel/2:_: (s.k. 2) Whose absorption etc. and one must be concerned they will absorb etc. — meaning that all the time the vessel expels it does not absorb; but a vessel whose absorption is slight one must be concerned that after finishing its slight expulsion it will absorb from another vessel that is still expelling. And see s.k. 6.
machatzit-hashekel/3:ב: Forbidden to boil them a second time — meaning if one kashered the vessels when the water was boiling, nevertheless one should be careful that the water not cease boiling all the time the vessel is in it, for after the water ceases boiling the vessel again absorbs from the hagalah water, even though the vessel is not ben yomo and there is also sixty in the water; nevertheless l'chatchila where possible one may not rely on this. And as written in s.k. 6; and even if one's intent is to boil them again — then again they will expel what the hagalah water absorbed — one may not rely on this where there is no need. Also one must be concerned not to be precise as required regarding boiling again, since he knows they already boiled once and will not consider that they again absorbed hagalah water.
machatzit-hashekel/3:ג: And so too Rashal in responsum siman 26.
machatzit-hashekel/4:_: (s.k. 4) That he not insert — so that it not absorb from the hagalah water, for hagalah water is kli sheini and absorbs; and since they are not yet boiling they do not act to expel to kasher; and this is an excessive stringency, for afterward when they boil, just as the vessels expel their own absorption they also expel the hagalah water they absorbed.
machatzit-hashekel/6:א: (s.k. 6) One must etc. that the vessels not be ben yomo — then even if there is not sixty in the water it is permitted, for they will not again absorb from the hagalah water, for the vessels are not ben yomo and noten taam lifgam; and even after four when chametz is already forbidden, nevertheless noten taam lifgam is permitted until night as above siman 447, and it is like noten taam bar noten taam d'heter.
machatzit-hashekel/6:ב: Sixty against it — then even if the vessels are ben yomo it is permitted, for the expulsion is nullified in the water; and even though we do not nullify prohibition l'chatchila, nevertheless here since one's intent is not to nullify but rather to remove the prohibition — it is permitted. And for this reason if the vessel is not ben yomo, even if there is not sixty it is permitted; and even though noten taam lifgam is forbidden l'chatchila. But if the vessel is ben yomo and also there is not sixty, even b'dieved hagalah does not help, for the hagalah water becomes forbidden and the vessels again absorb after their expulsion from the hagalah water; and even if one is careful that the water not cease boiling — then they do not absorb — and also one removes them immediately after they expel; and all the time they expel they do not absorb; nevertheless one may not rely on this, for perhaps one removes them immediately after finishing expulsion — and certainly one may not rely, for there is no fixed time but according to estimation, as Beit Yosef wrote in the name of Rashba; and also regarding that the water not cease boiling one may not rely, lest it ceased somewhat without his knowledge — so in Chokhmat Shlomo. For the prohibition returns and reawakens — for at first vessel A's expulsion taste was nullified when there was sixty against it and the taste of expulsion was not sensed in the water; nevertheless when one kasher vessel B, vessel B's expulsion joins with vessel A's expulsion and again the taste of expulsion is sensed in the water and the water becomes forbidden; for also in food if an olive of milk fell into sixty olives of heter and was nullified, and again another olive of milk fell into the sixty-one first olives — it too is nullified, and we do not say the first milk returns and reawakens — for we do not hold thus; nevertheless in vessels in our case one may rely on them.
machatzit-hashekel/6:ג: And Shach in Yoreh De'ah disagrees etc. and holds that vessel and food have one law — see there siman 121.
machatzit-hashekel/6:ד: And it appears to me that if vessel etc. as written Yoreh De'ah siman 98: a pot in which there is noten taam of sixty olives of heter and two olives fell into it, one of blood and one of milk — each joins with the noten taam olives of heter to nullify its fellow. And so noten taam of sixty olives of heter into which fell an olive of milk (per those who say regarding other prohibitions we do not say chanan), and in another pot there were thirty of heter and an olive of blood fell and they mixed b'shogeg — permitted since they are distinct tastes; and the same here.
machatzit-hashekel/6:ה: And in Chokhmat Shlomo he wrote it is not comparable to there, and these are his words: there it speaks of two prohibitions nullifying one another because each is a prohibition in itself; not so here where both their prohibitions are because of chametz taste absorbed in them — if so the name of chametz prohibition is on both of them, and how will they nullify one another? And it appears one should not be lenient in this — end of his words. However Magen Avraham's view is that it does not depend on their being two forbidden types but on their tastes being distinct; and so the Rosh brought in Shach there s.k. 33: it is logical that any prohibition is nullified when it cannot give taste in heter, and blood taste and milk taste are not equal — behold the milk taste is nullified in sixty and blood taste in sixty; what difference to me prohibition nullifying prohibition or heter nullifying prohibition — only that the taste of prohibition be nullified and it no longer have power to give taste in heter — end of his words. And even though here between a meat vessel and fish vessel the hagalah is because of chametz taste absorbed in them — nevertheless also the taste of prohibition is equal, for both are chametz taste. It must be that Magen Avraham's view is that chametz taste absorbed in meat changed its taste through the meat, and so chametz taste in fish changed through the fish — if so the two chametz tastes are not equal and they nullify one another.
machatzit-hashekel/6:ו: And one should kasher first — and this is only a stringency l'chatchila; for what of it that vessels of slight absorption after finishing expulsion will absorb from another vessel — we do not rely on the water boiling as above; nevertheless the vessels are not ben yomo or there is sixty in the water and also the absorbed matter expels as a vessel of great absorption expels; and nevertheless they are stringent l'chatchila. And so what is written: and one should not leave too long — they are concerned that after finishing expulsion it will again absorb from hagalah water; and this too is only a stringency l'chatchila; for what of it — for from this reason it requires sixty in the water or the vessel not be ben yomo; but whatever is possible to do so we need not rely on noten taam lifgam or on there being sixty — we do, for we do not nullify prohibition l'chatchila; and even though here one does not intend to nullify, nevertheless Taz wrote Yoreh De'ah siman 137 s.k. 4 that where possible in another matter, even though one does not intend to nullify prohibition — nevertheless it is forbidden.
machatzit-hashekel/6:ז: And one kasher the pot first and last — hagalah first because the pot absorbed chametz and there is not in what is in the vessel sixty against the vessel as explained in Shulchan Aruch Yoreh De'ah — if so the water in which one kasher vessels becomes forbidden from absorption of the pot; and so too when the vessels finish expelling they absorb from hagalah water forbidden because of the pot. And also at the end after finishing hagalah one must kasher the pot if one wants to use it on Pesach, for again the pot absorbed from hagalah water; and from this I did not understand what Taz wrote s.k. 5: and for this reason it appears also that one who comes to kasher a forbidden knife in a pot on the fire that is large and has sixty up to the knife may take a kosher pot for this and it is not nullifying prohibition l'chatchila — end of his words — for regarding the vessel one kasher we say this reasoning that it is not nullifying because one's intent is not to nullify; but regarding the vessel in which one kasher — we do not say so, for even though one kashered the pot first one must kasher it also at the end; even though through the first hagalah the pot is kosher, nevertheless one must kasher at the end — specifically regarding the vessel one kasher, since it is impossible otherwise; not so vessels one kasher in it — here it is possible to kasher again; and the same in a pot; and it is forced — Taz deals with an earthenware pot that has no remedy in hagalah — what of it — nevertheless it is called l'chatchila; who forced him to kasher in an earthenware vessel? However his intent is per the custom that one does not kasher ben yomo vessels — if so necessarily the forbidden knife is not ben yomo; and if so in such a pot if one kashered first one need not kasher at end since the vessels are not ben yomo, as Magen Avraham wrote. However per this view also sixty was not needed in the pot against the knife — and why did Taz require sixty in the pot if he goes per the custom that nevertheless they are stringent in all stringencies as Magen Avraham wrote — also in this it was not placed for my humble opinion. Kaf HaChayyim wrote in the name of Terumat HaDeshen and Agur: when one inserts the vessel into the pot to kasher it, even though the water is above boiling, nevertheless through this insertion the water ceases boiling; therefore one must be careful not to kasher quickly until one sees the water boiling again; and see there what he wrote to resolve the custom. However in any case one must leave them at least the measure of expulsion according to estimation.
machatzit-hashekel/6:ח: On siman 447 etc. — not as one who asked for those who hold it returns and reawakens on Pesach; if so of what use is hagalah if there is sixty in the water? Nevertheless on Pesach it returns and reawakens and then it is in any amount; and per Magen Avraham's reason in general taste — all agree it does not return and reawaken — end of his words.
machatzit-hashekel/7:א: (s.k. 7) One must be careful etc. — see Yoreh De'ah, meaning there the Mechaber wrote: a meat bowl rinsed in a pot of milk etc. even though both are ben yomo — permitted, for it is noten taam bar noten taam d'heter; and Shach challenged from Rabbeinu Yehuda's words here. Therefore he wrote there for b'dieved and here he wrote one must be careful l'chatchila.
machatzit-hashekel/7:ב: And this is that l'chatchila one is concerned for Rama's view there who wrote that in such a case taste of two substances is forbidden — the bowl received meat taste and the heter expels taste into the water, and the pot received milk heter taste and expels taste into the water; if so in the water there are two tastes of meat and milk mixed and the second taste is forbidden and they return and are absorbed in the vessel; if so here b'dieved depends on the dispute of Rabbeinu Yehuda and Rama there.
magen-avraham/1:א: If the vessels ben yomo — that even though the vessel is ben yomo and there is not sixty in the water against it, nevertheless it is permitted because it is noten taam bar noten taam d'heter, which is not so after the fifth hour. It is difficult — for above in siman 447 seif 5 the Rama forbids things cooked and did not permit from noten taam bar noten taam; and why does he permit here l'chatchila? One may say that here since there are many taste transfers from food to vessel and from vessel to water and from water to vessel — it is permitted.
magen-avraham/1:ג: However many dispute etc. — the words of the Rama are puzzling, for Rabbeinu Yehuda also agrees to this except that after its prohibition, once the water ceases boiling it is forbidden to boil them a second time, for all the time they are boiling they did not absorb from hagalah water; and if they ceased boiling they absorbed; but before the time of prohibition it is permitted, for it is noten taam bar noten taam d'heter; and so in Peri Megadim; and so Rashal in responsum.
magen-avraham/1:ו: One must be careful in all etc. — meaning one should see that the vessels not be ben yomo; and if they are ben yomo there must be sixty in the water against it; and if one kasher many vessels one after another there must be sixty against all, for the prohibition returns and reawakens (Beit Yosef and Darkei Moshe in the name of Rashba siman 462); and in Orach U'Mussar Shaarei Nitzchon wrote that b'dieved it is permitted, for some say also in food it does not return and reawaken, and if so in vessels one may be lenient; and so the Acharonim and Shach Yoreh De'ah siman 99 disagrees with them — see there. And it appears to me that if one vessel absorbed meat and the other fish it does not return and reawaken since they are distinct tastes, as written Yoreh De'ah siman 98. And one should kasher first vessels of slight absorption and afterward of great absorption; and one should not leave them too long; and the water should not cease boiling; and one should kasher the pot first and last. It appears to me that if the pot is not ben yomo one need not kasher it first, for it is no worse than the vessels themselves; and if one kashered it at the beginning one need not kasher at the end, for the vessels are not ben yomo; nevertheless the practice is to be stringent in all stringencies even before the fifth hour — so too Bach. And requires study why the Rama specified after six, for even after four one must be careful as stated, for even though the prohibition is d'rabbanan, nevertheless noten taam bar noten taam does not apply — see siman 447 seif 3 that regarding something containing only chametz taste we do not say it returns and reawakens — not as one who asked.
magen-avraham/1:ז: And last — when one kashered at the beginning or end.
magen-avraham/2:ג: Any ben yomo vessel — even alone and before the fifth hour, and even if there is sixty, because of a decree regarding a forbidden vessel that hagalah does not help all the time it is ben yomo, for it returns and absorbs from hagalah water and noten taam bar noten taam does not apply. And even counters one should scrub well and wait after scrubbing twenty-four hours so they not be ben yomo, and dried from cold water lest they be cooled from boiling ones; and be careful to pour on them quickly, not by throwing in air, for that is not considered irui (see Yoreh De'ah siman 92); and be careful to pour from the vessel in which one boiled the water and not draw with another vessel from the pot and pour on them to kasher, for that is kli sheini (and Avnei Nezer Yoreh De'ah 92 elaborated on this); however if one leaves the vessel with which one draws inside the pot until the water raises boiling in a small pot — then it is properly kli rishon (all this in Maharil); and Mateh Moshe wrote to kasher three days before Pesach; and all this depends on custom. Written in Shaarei Chaim siman 470: a Torah scholar expert in hagalah should kasher.
magen-avraham/6:א: One makes a lip — because it is impossible that boiling not splash on it once, and perhaps at the time of hagalah it will not splash on it; therefore one makes a lip; and even though the water drips through the clay — we hold as it absorbs in sparks so it expels in sparks (Gemara); and Maharil wrote: if it is a vessel with which one draws boiling water it has no remedy in this manner, for the outer side was not kashered; therefore one must insert it entirely into the pot. A vessel whose mouth is narrow so one cannot scrub inside, or that has cracks — forbidden in hagalah — end of his words. And it appears to me the same regarding bowls with which one covers the griddle — the outer side also needs hagalah.
magen-avraham/6:ב: Or one takes — meaning one fills it well at first.
turei-zahav/1:ב: If the vessels ben yomo — meaning they will return and absorb from what they expelled; and similarly if one leaves them too long. It implies that leaving a little there is no concern. Tur wrote: the practice is to insert and remove immediately — it appears he does not literally mean immediately but at least some waiting is needed; and so in Kol Bo one must be precise not to hurry removing the vessel from the pot so there is time for boiling to enter and expel what was absorbed; and there is no concern at all for leaving a little, especially since one kasher before the fifth hour.
turei-zahav/1:ד: Until Pesach when chametz is in any amount — because of chol ha-moed he needed this reason, for on Yom Tov itself, even on other Yamim Tovim, it is forbidden to kasher, as siman 509.
turei-zahav/1:ה: One must be careful in all etc. — requires study, for there is another matter not mentioned here — if one kasher part of the vessel twice; in this one need not be careful if one kasher before the fifth hour, as siman 451 seif 9; automatically after prohibition one must be careful in this; and how is it possible to be careful, for in the place one holds the vessel by hand while kashering water does not enter there, and all the more if one holds with tongs one must rotate the vessel and return it to the pot — and if so it is impossible not to kasher one place twice, impossible to narrow this; Beit Yosef brought that one should narrow per his ability, and truly this narrowing is impossible; therefore one must kasher then in a net called hovev, whereby one can kasher in one time since water enters all of it; but if one kasher after prohibition by hand or tongs hagalah did not succeed at all even b'dieved, for it returns and reawakens; and one may say if the vessel is not ben yomo one may kasher even by hand, for it is noten taam lifgam and permitted until night — this is not so, for in any case noten taam lifgam is forbidden l'chatchila as Yoreh De'ah siman 103; also not leaving inside does not help, for since nothing remains in the vessel to expel — it already expelled the first time — it certainly absorbed even immediately when inserted again; but if there is sixty in the pot water against the vessel one kasher, it helps also for kashering the vessel twice; but thereby one cannot kasher two vessels, for sixty would be needed against both, as Beit Yosef in the name of Rashba even afterward; and one may say it is nullifying prohibition l'chatchila, for one does not intend to nullify prohibition of what is absorbed but on expulsion of what is in it; and for this reason it appears also that one who comes to kasher a forbidden knife in a pot on the fire that is large and has sixty up to the knife may take a kosher pot for this and it is not nullifying prohibition l'chatchila; and per my words it resolves why he did not mention here kashering part of a vessel twice, since he mentioned here sixty against the vessel — not so above siman 451 seif 9.
turei-zahav/1:ו: Before six — meaning per the girsa I mentioned in s.a. that reads fifth hour; and the distinction between hagalah and libun that in hagalah something always remains.
turei-zahav/2:א: One of them is not ben yomo — one may say that when not ben yomo it is forbidden l'chatchila, for it receives impaired taste. One may say that here it is not certain the vessel will absorb since it is busy expelling — therefore there is no certain l'chatchila prohibition; but if it already finished expelling completely it certainly absorbs immediately when returned to the pot — then there is l'chatchila prohibition to kasher one place twice, as written.
turei-zahav/6:א: A large vessel etc. — meaning one wants to kasher it and is concerned perhaps there is chametz on its lip where water does not reach; and the same for a pot after one kashered vessels in it and wants to use on Pesach — one must make a lip; but initially before kashering vessels and kashering the pot first from prohibition in it — one need not make a lip, for regarding hagalah of vessels done in it there is no concern either way: if water power does not reach the lip to kasher it, also the lip absorption has no power to expel and absorb in vessels kashered by water; and if water has power to expel from there — then boiling in the pot also helps the lip to kasher it; not so in kashering a pot after hagalah — we certainly are concerned perhaps water did not reach the lip in all places it already received, and afterward when one cooks in the pot on Pesach one fills it and the lip forbids the cooked food; therefore one must make a clay lip; and so Tur words in the name of Geonim: rinse a large pot, kasher in boiling, kasher it, rinse in cold, expel first from chametz, then boil boiling water without measure (meaning one need not fill it except as needed for kashering vessels), kasher in it small pots and knives and wooden spoon and vessels needing hagalah in kli rishon; and be careful the water not cease from boiling, for if they cease it is forbidden to kasher in them and noten taam lifgam; rinse in cold; afterward fill the large pot, surround its lip with clay, and kasher per the first method and pour and rinse — end of his words; behold one need make clay only for what one wants to kasher afterward for Pesach; but initially when coming to kasher the pot to kasher in it — one did not need this, for the reason I mentioned; and even though Tur wrote at end per first method — this refers only to hagalah not the lip; and now the practice is to make first also a clay lip or insert a stone, and this is on the better side lest the kashered vessel touch the pot lip; and so concludes my teacher and father zl.
turei-zahav/6:ב: And the water reaches its lip — we say in the Gemara regarding this: as it absorbs through sparks so it expels through sparks — Rashi explained they do not absorb except through sparks that boiling splashed there, and it was not inserted into another pot at time of prohibition absorption; so at time of expulsion, even though not inserted into another pot, since it filled well and raises sparks on its lip — it expels; however Gednafa requires, for otherwise perhaps sparks do not ascend on the lip this time; but prohibition was cooked in it many times, and if it did not raise sparks every hour it raised once — end of his words; it implies where chametz entered inside the pot, boiling alone does not kasher it, but specifically to insert it into a pot to kasher it — a great rule: as its use so one kashered it. Mateh Yehuda zl wrote: accordingly bowls inverted sometimes on the griddle or drawn from the pot with a bowl, as he wrote in his heart — one must kasher it by inserting into another pot; but to pour boiling from kli rishon on them, even placing white-hot stones on them — all this is called only irui, not kli rishon — end of his words; and this stringency with white-hot stones is not from law but general stringency, for Shulchan Aruch siman 451 seif 6 wrote this kashering is hagalah in kli rishon; and Rama brought there seif 5 on large bowls to place white-hot stones etc.; therefore certainly this helps for all needing hagalah in kli rishon, provided boiling goes over all of it and its sides. Beit Yosef wrote: it appears to me per what our rabbi wrote in the name of Rosh requiring kashering the large pot — specifically when vessels kashered in it were ben yomo and there was not sixty in the water against them and hagalah was after four hours which is chametz prohibition time; not so if the pot was kashered before kashering in it — one need not return and kasher it — end of his words; and it appears one should be stringent l'chatchila also in this, for the essence of permission is because it is noten taam bar noten taam d'heter; we already mentioned Yoreh De'ah siman 95 seif 1 in the name of Semak that it is forbidden l'chatchila to make noten taam bar noten taam, and forbidden to cook fish in a meat vessel so afterward one eats with kutach — so too forbidden l'chatchila the pot and relying that it will be noten taam bar noten taam; one may say this is to kasher a vessel that is not ben yomo with a ben yomo vessel, as seif 2 there — absorption is not certain since the vessel is busy expelling — perhaps it did not absorb at all, as written there; not so here in a pot that certainly absorbs from vessels kashered in it, for it is not removed from them always — expulsion of the vessel remains — therefore forbidden l'chatchila; and so the practice is to kasher the pot after hagalah in all ways; and sometimes when there is prohibition in vessel expulsion, since it is possible to kasher it — one does not refrain. Mateh Yehuda zl is stringent because it is possible to wait twenty-four hours — this is insufficient, for vessels he kasher on erev Pesach before prohibition time and he needs them for Pesach; but b'dieved if one used it on Pesach it is not forbidden even in a case where vessels were kashered in it, in my humble opinion. Women practice not to use a pot into which they pour boiling on the stone with which they kasher vessels, because chametz smell entered it; yet there is no smell or taste — no prohibition at all on Pesach.
